subject.title: feat(gmail): add --inline and --text content modes to gmail attachment

question: Should this PR add in-process parsing of attacker-controlled PDFs, or should `--inline` land alone while `--text` is deferred?
rationale: Tests and a goroutine timeout cannot decide or eliminate the permanent parser trust and availability boundary, so repository-owner intent is required.

options.title: Land inline only
options.body: Split out `--text` and merge the low-risk base64 mode without adding an attachment parser.

options.title: Isolate PDF parsing
options.body: Keep `--text` after moving PDF extraction behind a killable execution boundary with hard resource limits.

options.title: Accept in-process risk
options.body: Merge both modes and explicitly own the possibility that timed-out parser work remains alive.

recommendation.title: Land inline only
recommendation.body: Split out `--text` and merge the low-risk base64 mode without adding an attachment parser.

likelyOwner.reason: The release integrator is the best available owner for deciding whether an untrusted-document parser belongs inside the CLI process.
